title: Shan States
capsule: The Shan States were a constellation of Tai-speaking principalities (mong) in the upland valleys of what is now eastern Myanmar, whose rulers (saophas) held autonomous power and paid tribute to successive lowland Burmese kingdoms from the 13th century onward. In the 14th and 15th centuries several Shan confederacies wielded enough power to dominate the Irrawaddy valley: the Mohnyin and Mogaung Shan sacked Ava repeatedly and controlled northern Burma for much of the period 1400–1527. King Bayinnaung of the Toungoo dynasty decisively subordinated the Shan saophas beginning in 1555–1563, incorporating their territories into a centralized Burmese imperial structure, effectively ending the period of Shan political independence represented in our dataset.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The boundaries of individual Shan mong are poorly documented; territory is reconstructed from Burmese chronicle accounts of tribute relations and military campaigns rather than administrative surveys, making precise borders highly conjectural.
